facts.fact: The Ministry of Information and Communication Technology contributed N$115 million over three years towards the Universal Service Fund, per CRAN's report for the year to 31 March 2025.

The Fund was established under section 56 of the Communications Act with levy regulations finalised, was officially launched on 19 March 2025 with N$115 million from the Ministry over three years, and its first bidding round allocated almost N$31 million of capital subsidies to MTC for nine sites.

note: CRAN's own regulatory levy income (N$25.5m loss year) is the regulator's licence income, not assigned to digital programmes: other, no fact. The page gives N$115m, whereas The Brief gives N$145m for the same event.

facts.fact: The government allocated N$145 million over three years as seed funding for the Universal Service Fund, announced by the Minister of ICT at the launch.
At the Fund's launch the minister announced the state seed funding, and CRAN had already disbursed a N$31 million subsidy to MTC for nine network sites.

note: Figure is N$145m here against N$115m in CRAN's reports; each recorded as stated. The MTC subsidy is a payment out of the Fund, recorded under acted.

facts.fact: Regulations made under section 56(2) of the Communications Act impose a universal service levy on every licensee of up to 0.5 percent of annual turnover, with a N$500 minimum, payable into the Universal Service Fund and effective on gazettal.

note: The regulations also let the Fund receive government money (the N$115m over three years) but give no amount spent or collected.
